by: midtown.html (RULING FV): the move library, written out from MIDTOWN.actors.moves — remake it after changing a move
note: counts: a loop's length in beats (once: played once over them, then held). midtown.html dances them; blocking.html offers them (its Dance button); tools/blocking-merge.py accepts these names. Each is described, with its source, in docs/hamilton-dance-moves.md.

step-touch.desc: step right, touch left beside it, step left, touch right

grapevine.desc: to the right: side, behind, side, touch; then back to the left

box-step.desc: right foot forward, left crosses over, right back, left to the side: a square

sway.desc: her weight side to side, arms floating

bounce.desc: a pulse: the knees dip on every beat (also "pulse")

clap.desc: the hands meet in front of her chest on every beat

point.desc: the right arm points up and out on 1, holds, comes down on 4

lunge.desc: the right foot forward into a lunge on 1, held, back on 4

kneel.desc: down onto the right knee over two counts, and stay there

rise.desc: up from a kneel to standing tall, the arms opening up and out

spin-quarter.desc: a quarter turn to her left on the spot (mirror: to the right)

spin-half.desc: a half turn on the spot

spin-full.desc: a full turn on the spot, arms in, then out

reach-up.desc: both arms up over her head on 1, up on her toes, held

arm-sweep.desc: the right arm sweeps from low across her up to high on the right, the body turning with it

salute.desc: the right hand to her brow, standing tall, held

bow.desc: a bow from the waist: down by 2, held, up by 4; one hand across her, one behind

curtsy.desc: the right foot slides behind, the knees dip, a little bow; the hands out as if holding a skirt

freeze.desc: she holds the pose she had on its first count, still as a statue

slow-walk.desc: the walk in slow motion on the spot — one stride every four counts (reverse: the "rewind", the walk run backwards)

stomp.desc: a knee up on the "and", stamped down on the beat; right then left

jump.desc: down on 1, up in the air on the "and", landing on 2

kick.desc: a kick forward with the right leg, then the left

two-step.desc: the hip-hop two-step: out to the side and together, right then left, a bounce on every beat

march.desc: marching on the spot: the knees up in turn, the arms swinging straight

pulse.desc: a pulse: the knees dip on every beat (also "pulse")

my-shot.desc: "Just like my country I'm young, scrappy and hungry, and I'm not throwing away my shot": second position, reach out to the people, hand to the heart, the hand flicks out, the boxer's groove, the roundhouse punch, the shot snapped down

legacy.desc: the My Shot phrase as it returns at "Legacy" at the end of the show: the same, but the shot is thrown UP

imagine-death.desc: Yorktown, "I imagined death so much it feels more like a memory": a hand behind the head, a hand across the chest, chin up; a knee up and a punch for "on my feet, enemy ahead of me"; arms crossed for "if this is the end of me"

command.desc: Yorktown, "weapon in my hand, a command, and boom": the rifle overhead, the forearm across the face, fists up and shoulders squared, the hands on the epaulets

heartbeat.desc: Yorktown, thinking of Eliza: a contraction on each "boom" of the heartbeat, then a point to the head

hiphop-march.desc: Yorktown, "we gotta go, we gotta get the job done": a hip-hop step like a march — out with the arms wide, the shoulders brushed off, a foot pushed out, down

musket.desc: firing a musket that weighs 35 pounds: a wide stance, the back used, aim, and the recoil through the whole body on the beat

hoist.desc: Hurricane: what she carries hoisted overhead, arms straight up, like the storm lifting it (a carried prop rises with her hands)

upside-down.desc: Yorktown, "the world turned upside down": furniture lifted overhead and turned upside down, held there (a carried prop flips over)

shimmy.desc: The Room Where It Happens: Burr's ego mocking him — the Fosse-like upper-body shimmy, knees bent and turned in, jazz hands, the head cocked

jazz-roll.desc: The Room Where It Happens' "ooey-gooey jazz": a slow hip roll, the shoulders sliding against it, the hands drifting up and down

crawl-back.desc: Hurricane, the "cockroaches": on hands and knees, crawling backward in slow motion (travelling, she turns her back to her path, so she crawls backward along it)

gavotte.desc: Helpless / Satisfied: the formal court dance — upright, up on the toes, one palm raised to her partner's, step and close each way (mirror her partner)

grind.desc: Helpless: twenty seconds after the palms touched, "they want to grind" — the hips rolling low, the arms round a partner

equals.desc: The Schuyler Sisters, "…that all men are created equal": the forearms held level one above the other in front of her — an equals sign

work.desc: The Schuyler Sisters, "…include women in the sequel. Work!": a hand up (the two fingers), the other on the hip, the hip popped

wall-ooze.desc: The Reynolds Pamphlet, round Angelica: slow motion into an invisible wall, the hit, then oozing down and out of it

bojangles.desc: Fred Astaire's "Bojangles of Harlem" (one in front, many behind doing the same): a heel dig forward each beat, the arms swinging, a clap on the "and" of 2

bullet.desc: The World Was Wide Enough, the Bullet: walking in slow motion, one arm out ahead carrying the bullet toward him (one stride every four counts; the path carries her)

row.desc: the rowers at Hamilton's death (and the duellists' boats): kneeling, a long stroke — reach forward, pull to the chest, lean back, recover

rewind.desc: Satisfied's rewind: the slow-motion walk run backwards (the slow walk with reverse); travelling, she turns her back to her path

aim.desc: a pistol arm levelled at the target straight ahead, the elbow locked, the head down the arm; on 2 the other hand comes up under it to steady it; held

aim-up.desc: the pistol arm thrown straight up, pointing at the sky, the other arm down at her side, the chin up; held (the duel: he fires into the air)

point-down.desc: the right arm thrust down and forward at 45 degrees, pointing at the floor, the left fist on the hip; on 1, held

point-fall.desc: the point straight at him on 1, held; on 3 the chest caves and the body is thrown back half a step as if shot, the arms flung forward and dropping; upright again on 4, half a step back (the ensemble as the book changes hands)

beckon.desc: the right arm out toward someone at chest height, palm up; the hand curls in toward her on each count, the head tipping toward them

shoo.desc: the right hand up at chest height, palm out, flicked outward from the wrist three times over the two counts, the head turned away

air-quotes.desc: both hands up beside the face, palms forward, the fingers flexed twice on 1 (the quotation marks), held up through 2

finger-wag.desc: the right forearm up in front of her, the finger raised, wagging side to side twice a beat; the left fist on the hip

make-it-rain.desc: the left hand holds a stack of bills at her chest; the right hand, just above it, flicks them out and down on every beat; the knees bouncing

angel-wings.desc: both arms spread wide behind her, a little above the shoulders, wrists leading; they beat twice like wings on 3 and 4, then are held spread (standing behind someone, as her wings)

breath.desc: a slow breath in: the chest lifts, the chin rises, the shoulders go back and the arms float a little out from her sides; held

gasp.desc: a sharp breath: a hand flies to her mouth and the other to her chest, the body jerks back; held

handshake.desc: the right hand out at waist height, pumped twice from the elbow on 1 and 2, held on 3 and 4 (with: the two meet face to face and their hands join)

coat-on.desc: into a coat: the arms back and down behind her into the sleeves on 1 and 2, a shrug of both shoulders on 3, the hands smooth the lapels on 4

sword-draw.desc: drawing a sword: the right hand crosses to the left hip on 1, draws up and out across her on 2, ends overhead and forward at 45 degrees on 3, held

sword-take.desc: taking a sword handed over: both hands reach forward low, palms up, on 1; the right closes on it on 2 and lifts it up before her on 3; held (with: the partner presents it on both hands, lets it go and bows)

gun-pass.desc: a pistol held out at full stretch, handle first, on the right palm with the left hand under it, and held out (with: the partner reaches in on 1, takes it by the grip and draws it back to her side on 2)

head-bob.desc: the head nodding on the beat: the chin drives forward and down on each beat and springs back on the "and", the shoulders loose, the knees giving

head-snap.desc: the head whips round to her left on the hit and holds there, the body still (mirror: to the right)

laugh-bob.desc: laughing: the head thrown back, the shoulders shaking three times a beat, the knees giving with it

chest-pump.desc: fists at the breastbone, the elbows back; the chest popped forward on every beat, the knees pulsing under it

shoulder-pop.desc: the shoulders pop up in turn on each beat, right, left, right, left; the elbows bent at the waist, a small knee bounce, the head bobbing

tootsie-roll.desc: the forearms rolling over each other in front of her on every beat, the knees in and out, the hips rolling side to side over the four

prance-fan.desc: a high-knee prance up on the balls of the feet, a knee up on every beat, the right hand fanning her face with a flick each count, the left wrist limp (mocking the court)

scrub.desc: on both knees, bent low over the floor, both hands scrubbing it side to side (the washerwomen)

lean-in.desc: the weight onto the front foot and the torso tipped forward toward someone (or a desk), the feet planted; held

fold.desc: folding to the floor: onto both knees, then sitting back on the heels, then the torso down over the knees, the arms on the floor ahead; held (the passed-out guest, the mourner, the hit)

hold-side.desc: wounded: the right hand clutching the left side of the ribs, the torso curled over it, the knees soft; held

floor-slide.desc: down onto the right knee on 1, then sliding 0.8 m to her right along the floor on 2 and 3, the arms swept back; held there (mirror: to the left)

floor-freestyle.desc: floor work, round and round: down to a crouch, a kick-through to sitting, rolled back onto the shoulders with the legs in the air, and up again to the crouch

strut.desc: a swagger on her own walk: chest up and leaning back, the shoulders rolling with each step, a bigger arm swing, the right hand swinging low (standing: the same swagger in time)

king-walk.desc: the King's mincing walk on her own path: small quick steps up on the toes, the chin up and the head held still, the hips swaying, the right hand raised with the wrist limp, the left at the waist

old-walk.desc: an old man's walk on her own path: stooped forward at the waist, short shuffling steps, a hand on the small of the back, the other on an imaginary cane, the head nodding

moonwalk.desc: the moonwalk: up on the ball of one foot while the other slides back flat past it, changing feet each count; travelling, she turns her back to her path and glides backward along it; standing, she slides back 0.25 m a count for three counts and glides back to her mark on 4

sit.desc: sitting: on the chair, bench, stool or box nearest her as the move starts (within 0.8 m), facing its front; with none there, where she stands at chair height; the thighs level, the feet forward, the hands on the thighs

comfort.desc: comforting someone seated: she stands close behind or beside her, one hand on her near shoulder, the head bowed (with: the seated one, who keeps her own sit)

lift.desc: the lead lifts the mate: a dip, then hands at her waist carry her 0.5 m up by 2, the lead's arms up under her, her legs trailing behind and her arms up; held, and down again over the entry's last count

catch.desc: the mate pitches forward, straight from her feet, the head and arms hanging; the lead behind her catches her round the waist by 2, leaning in after her; held, and drawn back upright over the entry's last count (the women in It's Quiet Uptown)

partner-lift.desc: a ballroom lift: the lead's hands at the mate's waist, she rises 0.55 m and turns a quarter in the air, one leg stretched behind, the other bent, the arms out; held, and down over the entry's last count

sabre.desc: swordplay: a fencing lunge with the right arm thrust forward on 1, recovered, then a parry across the body on 3, the free arm up behind (with: the partner parries the thrust and thrusts on 3, so the blades cross)
